items.q: They asked for 200 QPS. What arrived?
items.a: 38 on a small machine. Some single-process harnesses still topped out near 170 on a bigger one. The table still said the run happened. Ashok blames Python's GIL.

items.q: Where did 58 seconds of latency come from?
items.a: The benchmark client, thrashing while it collected streaming tokens. A 1,000 QPS run against a simulated server with no serving delay stayed flat once the client could scale out.

items.q: Why did one harness look 20% faster?
items.a: Temperature was 0. Their real workload sits near 0.7. The same ChatGPT dataset also produced different input-token counts because two tools sampled and truncated differently.

items.q: What does InferencePerf add beside server metrics?
items.a: Planned send time versus when the worker actually sent. They say it held 5,000 QPS and reported that it held. Prism then shows the sweep, not one QPS cell.
